question: Of the land animals killed for meat each year, roughly what share are chickens?
answer: About 90%. Of more than 80 billion land animals slaughtered for meat a year, roughly 75 billion are chickens. A beef animal yields hundreds of kilos of meat, a chicken under two. So a switch from beef to chicken, often made for health or climate, multiplies the number of animals killed per meal.
move: Count the cost of a choice per life affected, not only per kilo.
ask: When I weigh the cost of a habit, am I counting what I can see, or everything it touches?
trap: About a third, picturing the cows and pigs seen in fields.
source: Our World in Data, from FAO figures
